sam: Quick flag 406a7 onboarding Galeon9B int4. Our generative QA bench shows answer drift + sporadic token duplication in long contexts. Baseline FP16 looks fine.
li: can you paste a failing example + conversion details?
sam: failing prompt: `Article: ... mayoral race details... Q: who won?` ref: `Smith won the mayoral race.` pred: `Smith ... Smith ... in 2030` config: `quant=int4, backend=fastkern, rotary_scale=1.0 (runtime default)`, converter: `convert-galeon.py` (v0.9), tokenizer: SentencePiece v2 with upstream indicated NFKC.
anya: duplication + wrong year smell like phase drift + tokenizer normalization mismatch. Did converter carry normalization flags?
li: good point. Also check if model meta had headwise rotary_scale <-> >1.0. Some upstreams use 1.03 per-head for freq correction.
sam: I pulled the original checkpoint meta: `rotary_scale_headwise: 1.03` and `normalization: NFKC`. Our converted .idx had `rotary_scale: 1.0` and tokenizer defaulted to NFC during conversion.
triage-bot: tagging thread `regression/qa` and `priority:high`
li: run a quick A/B: runtime override `--rotary-scale 1.03` + set tokenizer.normalization=NFKC, disable kvcache warmup. See if duplication stops.
sam: running now. will queue small canary.
ml-ci-bot: queued job #galeon-int4-rotary-norm-canary
(8m later)
sam: Results: with rotary_scale=1.03 + NFKC -> duplication disappears on 28/30 failing prompts, hallucinated year fix on 25/30. With only rotary override (but NFC tokenizer) we still saw odd token splits causing slight semantic drift. With only normalization fix (NFKC) duplication reduced but not eliminated. So it's a combo: tokenizer normalization changes token boundaries, which interacts with rotary phase alignment under int4 to amplify drift.
li: that matches theory: different tokenization alters prefix lengths and positions where rotary phase applies; int4 quantization nonlinearity makes phase errors cascade. Also we saw kvcache logs: `kvcache: wrapped offset applied at head 3 -> warning`, warmup was applying per-head offsets which interact badly with headwise rotary scaling.
anya: actionable: 1) patch converter to preserve `rotary_scale_headwise` and `normalization` metadata; 2) add conversion unit tests that round-trip tokenizer normalization and assert identical token ids for canonical inputs; 3) short-term runtime: introspect model metadata and apply rotary_scale/headwise automatically if present, and prefer model-specified tokenizer normalization on load.
li: add a runtime flag `--kvcache-deterministic-warmup` that prefetches caches without applying offset wrapping corrections to keep behavior consistent between runs.
sam: I'll open a PR with the converter fix + unit tests, and a separate runtime PR for metadata-driven overrides + kv warmup flag. Will attach failing prompt set and evaluation logs.
ml-ci-bot: job #galeon-int4-rotary-norm-canary finished: 2 failed, 18 passed (canary). Logs: `/ci/jobs/6460005555/galeon-canary.log`
triage-bot: added issue links: `#ML-1248 converter: preserve headwise rotary and normalization`, `#OPS-887 runtime: metadata-driven overrides and deterministic warmup`
li: after PR lands we should run full QA sweep (summaries, open-domain qa, instruction-following) and add a new canary check that fails CI when ROUGE-L or EM drop more than threshold for model onboarding.
anya: also add a small smoke test in converter CI: convert -> load -> run 3 canonical prompts -> assert outputs exact match to upstream reference (hash-based). That would have caught this earlier.
sam: thanks. I'll assign reviewers and ping infra for broader canary resources. attaching repro snippet: ```bash
# repro
python -c "from runtime import load_model; m=load_model('galeon9b-int4', rotary_scale=1.03, tokenizer_norm='NFKC', kvcache_warmup=False); print(m.run('canonical_prompt'))"
```
li: perfect. scheduling follow-up review session tomorrow. :calendar:
